equipment_type: Electric duct heater / terminal reheat controller
applies_to: Neptronic electric duct heaters fitted with the HECB intelligent controller (staged and SSR, with optional EAS airflow sensing).
summary: The HECB controller runs Neptronic electric duct heaters and connects to BACnet MS/TP. The user guide lists 209 objects: system mode and occupancy, network setpoint and temperature inputs, demand and power limit, heat output and measured power, stage outputs, temperature limits, airflow status, cutout alarms and PID/configuration objects.
notes: The guide marks which objects exist in each control mode (external, internal, Neptronic signal, TPM, pneumatic...); MSV.100 shows the active mode.
MSV.103 Cfg_ObjectListMode (Integrator, Advanced, Factory) changes which objects are visible.
Footnote numbers printed after some names (for example HeaterDeltaTemp1) are removed here.
Objects marked "-" or "*" in the W? column are listed as read-only.

integration.summary: Set BV.1 SystemMode to Heat and MSV.2 Occupancy, then either write AV.1 SystemDemand (Network control mode) or, in internal control, AV.12 NetworkSetpoint with MSV.102 = Network setpoint and AV.14 NetworkTemp with MSV.101 = Network Temp. Read AV.3 HeatOutput, MSV.1 AirFlowStatus and BV.30 AL_GlobalAlarmMask.

minimum_points.name: AirFlowStatus
minimum_points.why: EAS airflow: no heat, no flow, low, regular

integration.enable: BV.1 SystemMode switches the heater between Heat and Off. MSV.101 and MSV.102 select where the control temperature and setpoint come from.
integration.heartbeat: When the setpoint and/or temperature source is Network, AV.105 Cfg_NetworkTimeout (1-15 min) is the time without BMS communication before the controller raises an alarm and turns the system off; AV.15 NetworkDowncounter shows the countdown, so keep writing the network values.
integration.remote_sensors: AV.14 NetworkTemp (with MSV.101 = Network Temp) and AV.12 NetworkSetpoint (with MSV.102 = Network setpoint) take BMS values in internal control mode.
gotchas: Some objects exist only in certain control modes or with EAS sensors / current transducers fitted.
